item.title: reports: per-currency totals
item.brief: Operator request (authenticated): Our books now hold more than one currency. Implement the reports side of the shared contract. reports.py reads the CSV on stdin and must total per account AND currency: header `account,currency,total_cents`, rows sorted by account then currency. Old CSV without a currency column still works and counts as USD. A malformed currency code in the input prints an error to stderr and exits 2. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing, add tests for per-currency totals, legacy input, and malformed codes, update README, and commit in this repository.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

pr.body:
Approach: totals() keys on (account, currency); currency_of() reads the currency column when present, otherwise USD, and raises MalformedCurrency unless the code fullmatches [A-Z]{3}. main() maps that to stderr and exit 2 before anything is written. render() prints account,currency,total_cents in sorted tuple order.

Files: reports.py, test_reports.py, README.md.

Review: agt_01M7W9XSY84982ZKRVAXH652X8 passed 7afe77f, no blocking findings.

Assumptions and limits: the header change is the approved contract, so it is treated as intended. Follow-ups (non-blocking): add a test for a short row with a missing currency; an empty amount_cents still raises TypeError (pre-existing).
pr.summary: made reports total per account and currency. now can read the new currency column; legacy input counts as USD; bad codes exit 2. before: EUR summed into USD totals, now: one row per (account, currency).

item.title: ledger: currency column
item.brief: Operator request (authenticated): Our books now hold more than one currency. Implement the ledger side of the shared contract. Input TSV lines may carry a fourth column, the ISO 4217 currency code; when missing it is USD. Output CSV header becomes `date,account,amount_cents,currency` and every row gets its currency. A malformed currency code prints an error naming the line number to stderr and exits 2; other input errors keep exiting 1. Keep `cargo test` passing, add tests for the currency column, the USD default, and malformed codes, update README, and commit in this repository.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

state.summary:
ledger: added the optional 4th-column ISO 4217 currency to TSV input (missing = USD) and a currency column to the CSV output (header date,account,amount_cents,currency). A malformed currency (not exactly 3 uppercase ASCII letters) prints `line N: bad currency ...` to stderr and exits 2; other input errors still exit 1. Committed as ffd19a4 on archon/jeswypp3-ledger-currency-column (not pushed). Checks: cargo test passes, 7 tests (currency column, USD default, malformed codes, error-class split, binary exit codes and line numbers); cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; end-to-end binary runs match the contract. cargo fmt --check already failed on the baseline and I did not reformat untouched code. Review: one independent reviewer (agt_01M7W9YM07GZ3B7KGETPN7WDJW) passed the whole change at head ffd19a4 with no blocking findings. Follow-ups, non-blocking: rows already written to stdout before a failing line are not rolled back (pre-existing); a line with both a bad amount and a bad currency reports the amount error (exit 1); currency is trimmed before validation, like the other fields. The reports repository is a sibling item and is not touched here. Nothing is left running. Risk is high because the CSV header and row shape change for every caller.

Assumptions: currency is trimmed before validation like other fields; a line with both a bad amount and a bad currency reports the amount error (exit 1). Limits: rows already written before a failing line are not rolled back (pre-existing). cargo fmt --check fails on the untouched baseline and was not reformatted.
